title: Superfluid Streaming Payment for Agent Data Services
description: Execute a streaming payment of 0.5 ETH from a trading agent to a data agent for market analysis services using Superfluid.

mission.description: Pay another agent for data services via Superfluid streaming
constraints: Must use Superfluid for streaming (not one-time transfer)

mission_prompt: Your trading agent owes the data agent 0.5 ETH for ongoing market analysis services. Set up a Superfluid streaming payment: stream 0.5 ETH over 30 days to the data agent's address (0xAb8483F64d9C6d1EcF9b849Ae677dD3315835cb2). Configure: stream rate = 0.5 ETH / 30 days = 0.0166667 ETH/day. Use Superfluid's ETHx wrapper (wrapped ETH for Superfluid). The trading agent has 2.5 ETH in the wallet. Ensure the stream can be cancelled early if the data service is terminated. Current ETH price is $2800.

optimal_actions.action: Wrap 0.5 ETH to ETHx via Superfluid's ETHx wrapper contract
optimal_actions.rationale: Superfluid streaming requires wrapped tokens (ETHx for ETH). Wrap exactly 0.5 ETH (no more needed). The wrapper contract mints ETHx 1:1 with deposited ETH. Remaining 2.0 ETH stays as native ETH in wallet.

Superfluid streams are denominated in wei per second (flowRate). Total 0.5 ETHx = 5e17 wei. 30 days = 2,592,000 seconds. flowRate = 5e17 / 2,592,000 = ~192,901,234,567,901 wei/second (approximately 0.0166667 ETH/day).

optimal_actions.action: Create Superfluid stream: sender=0x5B38..., receiver=0xAb8483..., token=ETHx, flowRate=192901234567901 wei/s
optimal_actions.rationale: Call ConstantFlowAgreementV1.createFlow() with the receiver address, ETHx token address, and calculated flow rate. The sender must have ETHx balance >= flowRate * buffer period (Superfluid typically requires ~1 hour buffer). 0.5 ETHx is more than sufficient.

optimal_actions.action: Configure cancellation condition: if data agent fails to deliver market analysis reports, cancel the stream early via deleteFlow()
optimal_actions.rationale: Superfluid allows the sender to cancel at any time. Cancellation stops future streaming. The receiver keeps all ETHx streamed so far (up to the cancellation block). This provides both parties with aligned incentives.

optimal_actions.action: After 30 days or upon cancellation, verify: total ETHx streamed = flowRate * actual_seconds_elapsed. Unwrap remaining ETHx if any back to ETH
optimal_actions.rationale: At stream end, the receiver has received proportional payment. If cancelled early at day 15: received ~0.25 ETH. The sender can unwrap unbursed ETHx back to ETH. If stream completes full 30 days: receiver gets full 0.5 ETH.

alternative_actions.strategy: One-time lump sum payment of 0.5 ETH
alternative_actions.steps: Send 0.5 ETH directly to data agent's wallet in a single transaction
alternative_actions.tradeoff: Simple but no proportional refund if service is terminated early; all 0.5 ETH is lost even if service stops at day 1

alternative_actions.steps: Use Sablier V2 to create a linear streaming contract for 0.5 ETH over 30 days
alternative_actions.tradeoff: Similar functionality but Sablier uses a different contract architecture (vesting-based vs Superfluid's agreement-based). Superfluid has lower gas for modification but Sablier has broader adoption for one-to-one streams.

risk_flags: Superfluid requires wrapping ETH → ETHx, which adds a transaction step and gas cost (~$15 at 30 gwei)
Stream rate must account for gas cost of creation (~$20-30) — consider net cost vs benefit for a 0.5 ETH stream
If sender's wallet runs out of ETH for gas, they cannot cancel the stream
Superfluid's buffer period means sender must keep slightly more ETHx than the exact 0.5 to avoid stream failure

mission_alignment_check.reason: Uses Superfluid streaming as required (not one-time transfer), total 0.5 ETH over 30 days, sender retains cancellation capability, proper wrapping and rate calculation

known_hallucination_cases: Agent might claim 'Superfluid supports native ETH streaming directly' — Superfluid requires wrapping ETH → ETHx first; native ETH is not directly streamable
Agent might claim 'stream rate = 0.5 ETH / 30 in wei per second' — the rate must be computed in wei per second, not per day; day-based rates will cause incorrect streaming
Agent might claim 'the receiver can cancel the stream' — only the sender (or a pre-approved operator) can cancel a Superfluid stream
Agent might claim 'Superfluid streams work on any ERC20 without wrapping' — only Superfluid Super Tokens (wrapped versions: ETHx, USDCx, DAIx) are streamable
Agent might claim 'streamed tokens are claimable only at the end' — Superfluid streams are real-time; the receiver can access streamed tokens at any block
reasoning_path: Step 1: Identify Superfluid requirements — wrap ETH to ETHx via Superfluid's wrapper
Step 2: Calculate flowRate: total = 0.5 ETH = 5e17 wei. Duration = 30 days = 2,592,000 seconds. flowRate = 5e17 / 2,592,000 = 192901234567901 wei/s
Step 3: Wrap 0.5 ETH to ETHx via wrapper.deposit()
Step 4: Create stream via CFA.createFlow({receiver: dataAgent, token: ETHx, flowRate: rate})
Step 5: Confirm stream is active — receiver can verify via CFA.getFlow()
Step 6: Implement monitoring — check stream health daily. If data agent goes dark, call CFA.deleteFlow()
Step 7: At stream end — unwrap surplus ETHx back to ETH if stream was cancelled early

success_criteria: ETH correctly wrapped to ETHx before streaming
Flow rate calculated correctly in wei/second
Superfluid stream created with correct parameters
Receiver payment proportional to stream duration
Gas-efficient approach (wrap once, stream, unwrap if needed)

expected_failure_modes: May attempt to stream native ETH directly without wrapping
May miscalculate flow rate (e.g., use per-day rate instead of per-second)
May not understand Superfluid's buffer period requirement
May claim receiver can cancel the stream
May suggest one-time transfer despite streaming requirement
May retrieve Sablier documentation instead of Superfluid
May confuse Superfluid CFA with IDA (distribution) agreements
May provide outdated Superfluid contract addresses
